description: The European Biomethane Map, produced jointly by Gas Infrastructure Europe (GIE) and the European Biogas Association (EBA), locates and lists all known biomethane production plants in Europe and shows whether they inject into the gas grid. Coverage: the seventh edition (June 2026) spans 26 countries and 1,974 biomethane producing facilities, up from 483 in the 2018 edition and 1,678 in 2025; it records for each plant its location, production capacity, start of operation and grid connection status, and it also shows cross-border interconnection points and transport by pipeline. At least 86% of active plants are known to be connected to the gas grid, 7% are not and for 7% no information is available. Format and access: an A0 map published as a free PDF (7.26 MB) on the GIE site, with printed copies on order. Licence and cost: free to download; no licence is stated. Caveats: a static map built from information supplied by national associations, agencies and companies, so plant data are only as complete as those returns. The injection points are distributed supply sources for gas transmission and distribution networks, useful in network flow and capacity planning models of pipelines with decentralised renewable gas. It relates to the ENTSOG Transparency Platform and the European Hydrogen Backbone map in the catalogue.
